report.paragraph: D2 MPDB PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE

GEOMETRY BASIS — Cap and wind datums derive from the selected Type F pad, 6-in pedestal and 36-in cap. Individual seat grades, separate plates, the retained wind envelope, terrain reference and gross pier-face width require final-detail confirmation.
FENCE WIND AND PIER NODE LOADS
Design basis: LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Edition (2024); FDOT Structures Manual, January 2026.
CALCULATION OVERVIEW

c.textvalue: Determine the wind loads transferred to the intermediate pier.
Fence geometry; tributary length; prescribed LRFD 13.8.2 fence pressure; bridge/direct-pier wind inputs.
Concurrent cap forces and moments, plus separate direct wall loads.

textcell.paragraph: CAP-REFERENCE RESULTS — SIMPLIFIED LRFD WIND COMPONENTS
• Fence load uses the single LRFD 13.8.2 gross-surface pressure; no projected-solid aerodynamic fence branch is used.
• For the qualifying girder bridge, LRFD 3.8.1.2.3a is used in lieu of the plan-angle sweep: 100% transverse plus 25% longitudinal, applied simultaneously.

report.paragraph: RESULTS PREVIEW | These are end results. The calculation execution begins at Step 1 below the strategy.
MODEL INPUT
• Use the complete simultaneous simplified load-set row; independent maximum components are not a load case.
SCOPE
• Included: global wind-load derivation and transfer to the cap reference.
• Separate: attachment design, bearing uplift, physical FE node assignment, and foundation capacity.
DESIGN BASIS AND ASSUMPTIONS
CALCULATION STRATEGY

The numbered strategy and blue calculation labels use the same seven steps. The fence itself uses the prescribed LRFD 13.8.2 gross-surface load; wind-speed pressure equations remain only where needed for the bridge concrete and direct pier wind.

section.name: FWStrategyStep01
section.paragraph: 1. Code basis, reference point, and directions.
• Use FDOT SDG 10.3 to select the wind-design route for this concrete girder pedestrian bridge: SDG 2.4.1 together with LRFD Section 3.8.
• Use the pier cap reference as the common point for all moments. T is across the bridge, L is along it, and V is upward.

paragraph.link: Go to Step 1: Code basis, reference point, and directions

section.name: FWStrategyStep02
section.paragraph: 2. Fence geometry and tributary length.
• Read the fence enclosure geometry from the Ped Bridge module and compute the vertical straight-leg height and cap-reference elevations.
• Use half of each neighboring simply supported span to obtain the bridge length whose uniform wind load reaches this pier.

paragraph.link: Go to Step 2: Fence geometry and tributary length

section.name: FWStrategyStep03
section.paragraph: 3. Prescribed LRFD 13.8.2 fence load.
• Use the LRFD 13.8.2 pressure of 0.015 ksf on the gross fence surface, including openings; for global bridge transfer, apply it once to the wind-exposed projected face for a given wind direction.

• Form one horizontal fence resultant and moment from that one-face projected load. Check the opposite wind direction by sign reversal; do not add a second simultaneous leeward pressure or a leeward reduction factor.

paragraph.link: Go to Step 3: Prescribed LRFD 13.8.2 fence load

section.name: FWStrategyStep04
section.paragraph: 4. Simplified superstructure wind components.
• Add the concrete superstructure wind to the prescribed fence resultant at the common cap reference and use the perpendicular-wind result as the transverse basis.
• Check the LRFD 3.8.1.2.3a span and height limits, then use 100% transverse and 25% longitudinal simultaneously instead of sweeping the plan-angle coefficient table.

paragraph.link: Go to Step 4: Simplified superstructure wind components

section.name: FWStrategyStep05
section.paragraph: 5. Wind acting directly on the pier.
• Use the FDOT/LRFD wind-speed pressure equation only for wind acting directly on the pier wall and cap.
• Keep direct wall forces separate from the cap-reference bridge-and-fence rows until they are paired to the same wind direction.

paragraph.link: Go to Step 5: Wind acting directly on the pier

section.name: FWStrategyStep06
section.paragraph: 6. Prepare the transfer to analysis nodes.
• Preserve each concurrent resultant while moving loads to physical analysis nodes.
• If a force is applied away from the cap reference, carry the residual couple needed to preserve equilibrium.

paragraph.link: Go to Step 6: Prepare the transfer to analysis nodes

section.name: FWStrategyStep07
section.paragraph: 7. Check the simplified method and complete the design handoff.
• Check geometry, tributary length, resultant equilibrium, the simplified-method qualification, and the 100%/25% component relationships.
• Hand off the simultaneous simplified superstructure/fence load set and the separate direct-pier wind components for FE analysis and the remaining design checks.

paragraph.link: Go to Step 7: Check the simplified method and complete the design handoff

section.name: FWCodeBasis
section.paragraph: CODE REQUIREMENTS AND MODELING ASSUMPTIONS

RFQ — Governing Regulations. The contract defines the applicable edition by Department adoption at advertisement, with later editions documented in the Task Work Order. We will retain this journal’s stated LRFD 10th Edition (2024) and January 2026 FDOT basis, and confirm them against that contract record. The listed Structures Manual modifications do not identify a replacement for SDG 2.4.1.A .

FDOT SDG 10.3.A–D . SDG 10.3 supplements the pedestrian-bridge guide. Paragraph A uses the SDG wind-speed table for pedestrian bridges. Paragraph B routes truss-type bridges to LRFD LTS and other bridge types to SDG 2.4.1 plus LRFD BDS. We will use the latter route for this concrete girder bridge. Paragraphs C–D identify when special wind analysis or Department review is needed; the Standard Plans 550-012 fencing exception must be checked against the actual proposed fence.

LRFD 3.8.1.1.1 . The main bridge wind module uses exposed bridge area for the concrete superstructure. The fence in this worksheet is instead loaded by the specific LRFD 13.8.2 metal-fabric fence provision.

FDOT SDG 2.4.1.A and Table 2.4.1-1 . The table replaces the LRFD wind-speed map for this purpose. Its Duval County value is 130 mph. We will use that design 3-second gust speed for Strength III. This is the specified design speed, not a claim that stronger winds are physically impossible.

LRFD 3.8.1.1.2 and Table 3.8.1.1.2-1 . The table gives 70 mph for Service I. We will calculate its pressure separately from the 130 mph Strength III pressure. The article also addresses higher speeds indicated by records or site-specific studies; a larger justified site criterion must be resolved in the design basis.

FDOT SDG 2.4.1.B and LRFD 3.8.1.1.5 . FDOT requires Ground Surface Roughness Category C unless Category D applies. We will use the adopted upwind terrain category to select the exposure calculation; Category D applicability depends on the actual site and wind direction.

FDOT SDG 2.4.1.C . Short code quote: “Use 0.85 for all load combinations and all structures”. We will use G = 0.85 for both bridge wind sets here. This FDOT provision replaces the LRFD gust table and definition; the accompanying commentary excludes ancillary sign, signal, lighting, ITS, and tolling supports from this wording.

LRFD Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-1 . The LRFD wind-pressure equation squares wind speed and multiplies by the unit constant, exposure-and-height factor, gust factor, and drag factor. In this worksheet it is used for direct pier wind; the concrete superstructure pressure is imported from the main bridge wind module. It is not used to generate a second fence pressure.

LRFD 3.8.1.2.1 and Eqs. 3.8.1.2.1-3 and 3.8.1.2.1-4 . Strength III uses the height-dependent Category C or D equation. Service I uses K_Z = 1.0 under the definition following Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-1 . We will retain the 33 ft minimum height. The main wind module uses the fence crown as a common exposure height; that common-height choice is a project assumption. The LRFD height definitions remain the basis for checking its applicability.

LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.1-2 . The table gives drag values used for the bridge concrete and direct substructure wind calculations. The direct pier calculation uses the bridge-substructure value C_D = 1.6. No mesh or fence-member drag coefficient is needed for the LRFD 13.8.2 gross-surface fence load.

LRFD 13.8.2 . The specified chain-link/metal-fabric fence pressure is 0.015 ksf acting normal to the entire surface. For this global bridge-transfer worksheet, that prescribed load is applied once to the gross projected fence face exposed for a selected wind direction. The opposite wind direction is a separate signed case. No second simultaneous leeward 0.015 ksf pressure and no leeward reduction factor are introduced because LRFD 13.8.2 does not provide a separate windward/leeward pressure pair. This projected-resultant treatment is the adopted global model for the curved enclosure; local fence-member and attachment design remains separate.

LRFD 3.8.1.2.3a . For usual girder and slab bridges having an individual span length not more than 150 ft and a maximum height not more than 33.0 ft above low ground or water level, the simplified wind components may be used in lieu of the plan-angle coefficient sweep: transverse equals 100 percent of the wind load for wind perpendicular to the bridge longitudinal axis, and longitudinal equals 25 percent of that transverse load; both act simultaneously. This worksheet checks the span and height limits live. For the height check, the bridge height is taken to the top of the concrete superstructure; the metal-fabric fence is loaded separately under LRFD 13.8.2 .

LRFD 3.8.1.2.3b and Commentary C3.8.1.2.3b . For direct pier wind at a skew angle, the article resolves pressure normal to each exposed face and applies the resulting components with superstructure wind. Short commentary quote: “all wind forces should correspond to wind blowing from the same direction.” The present wall table instead retains full face-normal component values as an envelope. That envelope is not yet a set of direction-resolved wall loads paired to every bridge row.

LRFD Table 3.4.1-1 . The WS load factor is 1.0 for the Strength III and Service I combinations shown here. We will use each separately calculated wind set in its matching load combination, with the required companion loads. WS means wind on the structure; this table entry does not mean all companion loads or all design checks have been included in this wind worksheet.

FDOT SDG 10.10.B and 10.10.F . For this concrete girder pedestrian bridge, the project engineer must design and detail the relevant attachment connections. Paragraph F calls for LRFD BDS and LRFD LTS in the listed attachment wind-design scope and refers back to SDG 10.3 . We will carry the global loads into the separate fence-member and attachment work; this worksheet does not perform those resistance checks.

LRFD 3.8.2 . The global projected fence model in this worksheet carries no separate vertical fence component; this does not complete the bridge-deck uplift check. For the current pier, Strength III deck uplift and its concurrent perpendicular horizontal wind are addressed in C001/C004 and the W2 entry set. Service IV is not used. Deck uplift is not included in the simplified cap tables in this worksheet.

textcell.paragraph: DESIGN BASIS QUICK REFERENCE
• GLOBAL BRIDGE WIND — FDOT SDG 10.3 routes this concrete girder pedestrian bridge to SDG 2.4.1 and LRFD Section 3.8.
• FENCE — LRFD 13.8.2 supplies 0.015 ksf normal to the entire metal-fabric fence surface; this is the only fence pressure used here.
• GEOMETRY — Semicircular enclosure geometry is retained, but the global LRFD 13.8.2 load is applied once to one wind-exposed projected face for each wind direction.
• SIMPLIFIED SUPERSTRUCTURE WIND — LRFD 3.8.1.2.3a permits 100% transverse plus 25% longitudinal simultaneously when the span and height limits are satisfied; this worksheet checks those limits live.
• DIRECT PIER WIND — Wind-speed pressure equations are retained only for the pier wall/cap and imported concrete wind.
• LIMIT STATES — Strength III and Service I are kept as separate WS = 1.0 wind sets.

report.paragraph: Moment that still must be applied after a force is moved above the cap reference.

section.name: EqNotes_FenceWind_045_M_residual_M_cap_F_z
section.paragraph: M_cap is the total required moment about the cap reference. F is the horizontal force being applied. z is the signed height of that force’s application point above the cap reference, using the same sign convention as the moment component.

Multiplying F by z gives the moment that the relocated force already creates about the reference. Subtract that amount from M_cap to find the remaining couple to apply. If the force is applied at the reference, z is zero and the full required moment remains.
This is a scalar force-and-moment balance for one matching direction pair. For several forces, their combined moment about the reference must be accounted for before assigning the remaining couple.

textcell.paragraph: MEANING OF PASS
• These checks establish geometry consistency and load bookkeeping; they do not establish member, connection, bearing, or foundation capacity.
• Confirm LRFD 13.8.2 fence applicability, the simplified-method span/height qualification, hoop geometry, cap reference, direct-pier wind direction mapping, and analysis-model axes before final use.
• Address attachment resistance, deck uplift, FE analysis, bearings, piles, and foundations in their designated calculations.
